page.title: Nextcloud Backup Destinations
page.subtitle: Back up containers to a Nextcloud instance via WebDAV (RFC 4918). Two auth modes: OAuth 2.0 refresh-token flow (with the operator creating an OAuth2 client in /settings/admin/oauth2) or direct app-password authentication (the operator generates an app password in Personal settings → Security). Chunked uploads use the WebDAV PUT stream with Content-Length + Content-Range; large uploads work because Nextcloud's WebDAV server supports chunked ranges server-side. Same Test round-trip shape (write / change / delete) as the SharePoint and Google Drive plugins.
page.registerHint: Click Test connection to verify the WebDAV endpoint is reachable and the credentials are valid. After the dialog saves, the plugin's Test runs write / change / delete against a uniquely-named folder under the configured base path.

fields.refreshToken: Refresh token (delivered by the OAuth consent flow)
fields.folderId: Folder under the user root (blank for the user root)

help.clientId: Optional. OAuth 2.0 client_id from Nextcloud admin → Settings → Security → OAuth 2.0 clients. Leave blank if you use an app password instead.
help.clientSecret: Either the OAuth 2.0 client_secret from your Nextcloud OAuth client config, or an app password generated in Nextcloud Personal settings → Security → App passwords. Both work over HTTP Basic auth on every WebDAV call.
help.refreshToken: After saving the destination, click Connect to grant account consent and store a long-lived refresh token.
help.folderId: Forward slashes are treated as folder separators. Intermediate folders are created automatically (MKCOL on each segment).

error.noSecret: OAuth client secret or app password is required.

form.introBody: Generate an app password in Personal settings → Security → App passwords, or register an OAuth 2.0 client under admin settings. Either approach works over HTTP Basic auth on every WebDAV call. McHarbor stores the secret encrypted at rest.

host.label: Nextcloud base URL
host.help: Base URL of the Nextcloud instance, e.g. https://cloud.example.com. Do not add a trailing slash — the plugin derives the WebDAV endpoint at call time.

username.label: Username
username.help: Nextcloud login (username or email). Used to scope the WebDAV path under /remote.php/dav/files/{username}/.

clientId.label: OAuth client ID (optional)
clientId.help: OAuth 2.0 client_id from Nextcloud admin → Settings → Security → OAuth 2.0 clients. Leave blank if you use an app password instead.

clientSecret.help: Two valid options: (1) the OAuth 2.0 client_secret from your Nextcloud OAuth client config, or (2) an app password generated in Nextcloud Personal settings → Security → App passwords. Both work over HTTP Basic auth on every WebDAV call. Stored encrypted at rest.

basePath.label: Folder under the user root
basePath.help: Optional subfolder under the user's Nextcloud Files root, e.g. Backups/2026. Leave blank for the user root. Forward slashes are treated as folder separators and intermediate folders are created automatically.

apiPath.label: WebDAV path prefix (advanced)
apiPath.help: Override the WebDAV path. Defaults to /remote.php/dav/files/{username}/. Set this only if your Nextcloud sits behind a reverse proxy that rewrites the WebDAV path. Leave blank unless you know what you're doing.

steps.s1: In Nextcloud, open Personal settings → Security → App passwords. (Admins can enable this for the whole instance via Settings → Security.) Give the app password a descriptive name (e.g. mcharbor-backups) and click Create app password.
steps.s2: Copy the username (the account you want backups to land under) and the app password Nextcloud just generated. Both are case-sensitive.
steps.s3: In McHarbor, paste the Nextcloud base URL (e.g. https://cloud.example.com — no trailing slash), the username, and the app password into the form on the left. Optional: set a folder under the user root (e.g. Backups/2026) and let McHarbor create intermediate folders automatically.
steps.s4: Click Test connection to round-trip a probe file in the resolved folder. The plugin performs an HTTP Basic-authenticated WebDAV PROPFIND against /remote.php/dav/files/{username}/ to confirm the destination is reachable and the credentials are valid.
steps.s5: Optional: when you're ready to switch to a delegated OAuth flow (so the operator doesn't have to manage app passwords), create an OAuth 2.0 client in Nextcloud admin → Settings → Security → OAuth 2.0 clients. Set the redirect URI to your McHarbor host's /api/storage-locations/oauth/callback. Generate a client secret, paste both into the form, then click Connect to grant consent. The plugin stores the refresh token and refreshes it transparently on every backup run.
steps.s6: Trigger a backup. The plugin uploads the archive via WebDAV using Content-Range chunked PUT so even 10+ GB backups stream without buffering the entire payload in memory at once. Nextcloud's WebDAV server reassembles the chunks server-side.
